post.description: Opening the bell: everything so far counts as read.

Pub/Sub pushes every event here. A failed email or Slack post answers with an error, so
Pub/Sub retries it, and moves it to the dead-letter topic after the subscription's maximum
attempts; neither Resend nor Slack gets the same message twice. Over Resend's per-second limit
(a burst of invites) it answers 429: Pub/Sub retries with backoff, and it isn't counted as a
server error. An event no retry can handle (one missing the data its email needs) is logged
and acknowledged (handle_or_drop).

Answered once the signature is checked and the event recorded (by its delivery id, so a
repeat is recorded once): its work runs from the email.webhook_received event
(services/webhooks.py), retried by Pub/Sub, not before the answer.

post.description:
Every minute for an hour each morning, from Cloud Scheduler: the activity digest. Each
run goes on where the last one stopped; nobody gets it twice in a day.

Every minute for an hour each morning, from Cloud Scheduler: reminders, each kind
at most once a week to a user. The sent log's old rows go too, and soft bounces past their
window, until CLEANUP_SECONDS after the run started; the next run deletes the rest.

Every minute from 08:00 to 18:59 UTC, from Cloud Scheduler: legal notices and campaigns,
each run going on where the last one stopped; nobody gets one twice.

Every minute, from Cloud Scheduler: publishes events that weren't published right after
their change.

AudienceGroup.title: AudienceGroup
AudienceGroup.description:
Whom a campaign goes to, besides everyone: the people who joined a company (members), who
took a company's interview (candidates, rounds' interview sessions) or a free practice round
(learners, rounds' practice sessions). Someone in several groups gets it once.

AudienceIn.title: AudienceIn
AudienceIn.description:
Whom a campaign of `kind` goes to: everyone (no `groups`), or the people in any of
`groups`; of companies, with `editors_only` only their owners and admins, and for an
important notice with `company_ids` only those companies'.

CampaignIn.title: CampaignIn
CampaignIn.description:
A campaign as a superadmin writes it, in English: a product update, an offer or an
important notice, whom it goes to, and the page on the site its button opens.

CampaignRowOut.title: CampaignRowOut
CampaignRowOut.description:
A campaign in the list: its English subject, whether every language has its texts, where
it stands (a draft, being sent, sent to everyone, or stopped) and once it's sent, its
counts.

CampaignTexts.title: CampaignTexts
CampaignTexts.description:
A campaign in one language: its subject (also the email's heading), its text (in Markdown:
the editor's bold, italic, links and lists) and its button's text.

CandidateOptOutIn.title: CandidateOptOutIn
CandidateOptOutIn.description: A superadmin stops a company's emails to the address, or lets them through again.

CompanyOptOutOut.title: CompanyOptOutOut
CompanyOptOutOut.description:
A company that invited an address, or whose emails it stopped: whether every email from
the company to it is stopped, whether a superadmin stopped them (only that can be lifted
there; the candidate's own stops stay), and for how many invites only the reminders are.

CountOut.title: CountOut
CountOut.description:
How many of something a service holds, for another service's internal call (a company's
working integrations, for its menu).

LegalChangeOut.title: LegalChangeOut
LegalChangeOut.description: A document's new version, noticed and applying from `version` (a day).

LegalNoticeState.title: LegalNoticeState
LegalNoticeState.description:
Where a document's current version stands: its email can be asked for, it already
applies, it's too close to the day it applies, or it was asked for (and is going out, or
went out).

NotificationOut.title: NotificationOut
NotificationOut.description: What the bell shows: `kind` picks the text, `data` fills it, `link` opens the page.

PushBody.title: PushBody
PushBody.description: What Pub/Sub sends to a push endpoint.

RecipientsOut.title: RecipientsOut
RecipientsOut.description:
Who the campaign would reach now: the users of its audience with an address, not
suppressed, and for an optional kind with its setting on; each once.

SendIn.title: SendIn
SendIn.description:
An important notice is sent only once the superadmin confirms it's about the service
itself, never a promotion.

SlackOut.title: SlackOut
SlackOut.description: The company's Slack channel as the page shows it: never its web hook.

SuppressionOut.title: SuppressionOut
SuppressionOut.description: The address's place on the suppression list; both None when it isn't on it.

UnsubscribeOut.title: UnsubscribeOut
UnsubscribeOut.description:
What a link stops, for the page to say before it's confirmed: the type, and for a
candidate's link the company's name.

UnsubscribeType.title: UnsubscribeType
UnsubscribeType.description:
What an unsubscribe link stops. A user's optional emails: one kind of the activity digest,
the whole digest, reminders, product updates or offers. A candidate's emails, sent on a
company's behalf: the reminders for one invite, or every email from that company.

UpdatesIn.title: UpdatesIn
UpdatesIn.description: The companies whose notifications to read, after `since` and up to `until`.

UserEmailIn.title: UserEmailIn
UserEmailIn.description:
An email address sent in the body, so request logs don't record it: the account's, in
accounts' calls to delete or export a user's data, or the one a superadmin looks up.
